what_happened: The job "Dispatch jobs from a stable ref so merges don't disturb running jobs" (20261018-113512-gvcs) failed during planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The approach was judged sound: remove the post-merge resync_onto_merge call, cut the pushed head with Git::replay so pull request diffs don't grow, and add a sidecar so reruns don't push again. The critic found one major gap. The cut lives only in GitRemote::cut_head, a trait method whose default is Ok(None), but every planned test goes through FakeRemote. So the criterion 2 diff assertion and the cut and fingerprint-refusal tests would either fail or test the double's own logic, not the production cut. Three minor findings: the replay range is unspecified; the non-fast-forward question is already answered by check_replace; and a tip moved by outside commits is always refused by the new fingerprint check, which the docs should say. One nit: values attempt() computes before building the client are not said to move into land_pr_with. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered. This is a retry of the same request that failed the same way in 20261018-095726-r3bn.
cause: The planning stage writes test demonstrations without checking that the code under test can be driven that way. Here the plan placed the production logic on a trait method that the test double bypasses. Nothing in the plan template makes the planner name, for each demonstration, the seam or harness it uses and whether it exists. A design rule is also missing: logic under test must not live where the fake replaces it. The critic can see this only by reading the code, so it surfaces late. The three-round cap does not require major findings to shrink and keeps no partial plan, so a late gap fails the job. A retry of the same request also starts without the previous critic's findings, so the known seam problem was found again.
prevention: Change the plan template and the planning gate. (1) Each demonstration must name its test seam: the fixture or harness, the production function it runs, and whether the seam exists or which step adds it. Logic under test must not sit behind a trait method or default that the named fake replaces. (2) A cheap check before the critic compares each named seam with the code, and fails the plan early if a demonstration depends on a fake that bypasses production logic. (3) A retry or re-ask of a failed planning job must start from the previous critic's findings, so known gaps are fixed in round 1. (4) The planning loop must say what happens when round 3 still has a major finding, for example keep the best plan and hand it to the operator or split the job. Any of these alone would have caught the cut_head gap in round 1.
proposed_request: Dispatch jobs from a stable ref so merges don't disturb running jobs. Outcome: after a job's pull request merges, Athena no longer resyncs running or queued jobs onto the new main (remove the post-merge resync_onto_merge call in Athena::land_pr and update land.rs), and each later job's pull request still shows only its own changes, not the content of earlier landed jobs. Constraints for the plan: put the head-cut logic (cutting the pushed head onto the remote tip with the existing Git::replay) in code shared by production and tests, or test it with GitRemote over a local bare repo. Do not rely on a FakeRemote whose trait default is Ok(None). State the replay range used by the cut. Do not tighten check_replace, which already allows non-fast-forward replacement under the expected-head check. Move the values attempt() computes before building the client into land_pr_with, and say so in the plan. Document that a tip moved by commits other than Athena's squashes is refused by the fingerprint check, which is how a stale job is handled. List gh.rs as a deliverable. Acceptance: a test that runs the production cut shows job B's pull request diff after A merges contains only B's changes; a rerun does not push again; a stale tip is refused; the existing checks pass.
